gaps.sentence: Don't worry, we still have ___ time before the gates close.
gaps.hint: positive meaning: there is some time; 'time' is uncountable
gaps.explanation: 'A little time' means some time, which reassures; 'time' is uncountable.

gaps.sentence: There weren't ___ chairs, so some guests had to stand.
gaps.explanation: 'Chairs' is countable and plural, so 'many' fits; 'much' and 'little' are for uncountables.

gaps.sentence: She gave the children two sweets ___.
gaps.hint: distribution per child at the end of the sentence
gaps.explanation: 'Two sweets each' means two per child; 'every' cannot stand alone here.

gaps.sentence: He was driving ___ fast for the icy road.
gaps.explanation: 'Too fast for something' means faster than is safe; 'so fast' needs a 'that' clause, not 'for'.

gaps.sentence: ___ everyone in the office passed the safety test.
gaps.hint: the only adverb that can modify 'everyone'
gaps.explanation: 'Almost everyone' is the standard pattern; 'each', 'all' and 'every' cannot directly precede 'everyone'.

gaps.sentence: There is so ___ crime in this area that people are afraid.
gaps.explanation: 'So much' is used with uncountable nouns like crime; 'plenty' would need 'of'.

gaps.sentence: We had a ___ of fun at the fair.
gaps.explanation: 'A lot of fun' is the fixed phrase; 'fun' is uncountable and the article 'a' forces 'lot'.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the two proposals has been approved so far.
gaps.explanation: 'Neither of the two' — 'none' is for three or more.
